verdict.rationale: Fly.io builds Machines from standard Docker images, can reuse a project's existing Dockerfile, generates one for mainstream frameworks, and says apps can ship from GitHub. However, the documented workflow centers on its own `flyctl`/`fly launch` CLI, and the evidence never shows CI pipelines or editor workflows working without it. missing for 10: documented CI integration (e.g., deploying from existing pipelines), evidence that deploys work without proprietary flyctl tooling, detail on the GitHub deploy flow, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Ship from GitHub or our CLI with `fly launch`.
If your project already has one, Fly Launch can use it instead.
we'll generate one for most popular frameworks, including Rails, Phoenix, Django, Node, Laravel, Go, Rust, .NET and more.
We build Machines out of the images you give us and we run them where you tell us to.
